prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Denver. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Denver for a dental implant?
competitors_mentioned: ClearChoice Dental Implant Center — Denver metro
engine_stated_criteria: Tooth needs extraction, you want sedation, or bone grafting may be needed
What implant system/brand do you use, and will I receive the implant record?
What portion, if any, is covered by my dental or medical insurance?
answer_verbatim:
For a single missing tooth or a few implants in Denver, I’d call **three different types of providers**: a periodontist or oral surgeon for the surgical evaluation, plus a restorative dentist/prosthodontist who will design and place the crown. Getting two consults is worthwhile because implant plans and quotes can differ substantially.

### Practices to put on your call list

1. **University of Colorado School of Dental Medicine — Patient Care Clinics, Aurora**
   - **Why call:** Strong choice for a complex case, second opinion, bone grafting, medically complicated patients, or if cost matters. CU’s dental school has specialty clinics in **periodontics, prosthodontics, and oral/maxillofacial surgery**, so the surgical and restorative sides can be coordinated.
   - **Best fit:** You want a teaching/faculty setting, a comprehensive plan, or potentially lower fees than a premium private office.
   - **Ask for:** An implant consultation through Periodontics, Prosthodontics, or Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery; ask whether the resident/faculty clinic or faculty practice is the best fit.

2. **Denver Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery (Denver metro)**
   - **Why call:** Oral and maxillofacial surgeons are especially useful if you may need an extraction, sedation, bone graft, sinus lift, or treatment after trauma/infection. A surgical practice is often the right first stop when the tooth is still present but failing.
   - **Best fit:** You need extraction plus implant planning, are anxious and want IV sedation available, or were told your bone level may be limited.
   - **Ask for:** A consultation that includes **CBCT/3-D imaging**, a written grafting plan if needed, and coordination with the dentist who will make the final crown.

3. **Colorado Periodontal & Implant Specialists (Denver/Cherry Creek area)**
   - **Why call:** Periodontists specialize in the gums and bone around teeth and implants. They are often an excellent choice when gum disease, recession, bone loss, or an esthetic front-tooth implant is involved.
   - **Best fit:** A front-tooth implant, history of periodontal disease, receding gums, or a desire for a surgeon whose practice is focused on implant tissue and bone management.
   - **Ask for:** Whether the surgeon places the implant and whether your regular dentist/restorative dentist handles the crown—or whether they have an in-house restorative team.

4. **Colorado Surgical Arts (Denver metro / nearby Front Range offices)**
   - **Why call:** Another oral-surgery option for a surgical second opinion, especially if you need extractions, grafting, sedation, or multiple implants.
   - **Best fit:** More involved surgery or if you want to compare a surgeon-led plan with a periodontist-led plan.
   - **Ask for:** The total surgical fee—including extraction, graft material/membrane, implant, abutment if applicable, sedation, and follow-up—not just the implant fixture price.

5. **ClearChoice Dental Implant Center — Denver metro**
   - **Why call:** Most useful if you are missing many teeth or considering a **full-arch fixed implant bridge** (“All-on-4”/“Teeth-in-a-Day” type treatment). Their model is built around surgery and final teeth in one organization.
   - **Best fit:** Full-mouth reconstruction, multiple failing teeth, dentures that are no longer working, or a desire for one office handling the entire case.
   - **Caution:** For one straightforward missing tooth, compare their quote with a periodontist/oral surgeon plus a high-quality restorative dentist. Full-arch centers can be excellent for full-arch cases, but may not be the most economical or tailored route for a single tooth.

## How I’d choose among them

- **One missing tooth, healthy gums/bone:** Start with a **periodontist** and also have your general dentist or a prosthodontist involved in planning the crown.
- **Tooth needs extraction, you want sedation, or bone grafting may be needed:** Start with an **oral and maxillofacial surgeon**.
- **Front tooth, gum recession, or gum disease:** Favor a **periodontist** or prosthodontist-periodontist team.
- **Several missing/failing teeth or dentures:** Include a **full-arch implant center** such as ClearChoice, but still obtain an independent specialist opinion.
- **Complex health history or a tight budget:** Include **CU School of Dental Medicine** in your comparison.

## Questions to ask every office

Use these questions on the phone and during the consultation:

1. **Who places the implant, and who designs/places the final crown or bridge?**
2. **Will I get a CBCT/3-D scan before the final plan?**
3. **Do I need extraction, bone grafting, a sinus lift, or gum grafting?**
4. **What is the all-in estimate?** Ask them to separate:
   - consultation and imaging  
   - extraction  
   - grafting  
   - implant fixture  
   - abutment  
   - crown/bridge  
   - temporary tooth  
   - sedation  
   - follow-up and warranty
5. **What implant system/brand do you use, and will I receive the implant record?**
6. **What happens if the implant does not integrate or if grafting is needed after surgery?**
7. **Will you coordinate with my general dentist, or do I need to arrange the crown separately?**
8. **What portion, if any, is covered by my dental or medical insurance?**

A good implant office should not give a final treatment recommendation without examining you and usually taking 3-D imaging. Also, be wary of ads quoting a very low “implant price” that excludes the abutment, crown, grafting, imaging, or extraction—the completed single-tooth treatment is what matters.
